summary: Sections behind headings: people open only the parts they need, which keeps long pages short. Four custom elements share state through context.

selection.note: single opens one item at a time; multiple lets any number be open.

collapsible.note: With selection=single, lets the open item be closed. Without it the open item's trigger is aria-disabled so one item always stays open. Ignored for multiple.

value.note: The open item value. With selection=multiple, a space-separated list of item values. Updated when a person opens or closes an item.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: sb-accordion: light-DOM wrapper that owns which items are open, moves focus between triggers and shares state through context. No shadow content of its own.

change.note: Fires on the sb-accordion host after a person opens or closes an item. detail.value lists the open item values. Not fired for changes made from code. A change from a form control inside the content also bubbles to the host: listen with event.target === host (that one has no detail).

open.trigger: item value is in the accordion value
open.note: Content height animates; the chevron turns 180 degrees.

disabled.trigger: disabled on the accordion or the item

accessibility.role: heading + button per item; region per open panel
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: Trigger text. The panel is named by its trigger.
accessibility.targetSize: Each trigger is at least 44px high with default padding (WCAG 2.5.8).

keyboard.ArrowDown: focus the next enabled trigger, wrapping to the first
keyboard.ArrowUp: focus the previous enabled trigger, wrapping to the last
keyboard.Tab: every enabled trigger stays in the tab order

aria: trigger: native button inside an element with role=heading and aria-level (level prop, default 3)
trigger: aria-expanded mirrors the item; aria-controls through ariaControlsElements to the content host (resolves from a shadow root to the light DOM above it)
selection=single without collapsible: the open item's trigger has aria-disabled=true

content: role=region named by its trigger through ElementInternals ariaLabelledByElements (ID references would not cross shadow roots); aria-label with the trigger text where the property is unsupported
closed content is visibility:hidden after the animation, so it is neither focusable nor read
aria-controls and the region's aria-labelledby are re-resolved when a trigger or content is added or removed later
heading level is clamped to 2-6 (a non-number falls back to 3)
item values must not contain whitespace (the accordion value is space-separated); a console warning fires once per item otherwise
forced colors: the chevron takes ButtonText

elements.summary: One collapsible section: a trigger and its content, with a bottom border.

value.note: Identifies the item in the accordion value. Must be unique within the accordion.

anatomy.name: item
anatomy.notes: Light-DOM block with the border; sets data-state to open or closed for its parts.

elements.notes: Must be a child of sb-accordion.

elements.summary: The heading and button that toggles its item, with a chevron.

level.note: Heading level of the wrapper (aria-level), 2 to 6. Pick the level that fits the page outline.

anatomy.name: chevron
anatomy.notes: Lucide chevron-down, decorative; rotates 180 degrees when open.

default.notes: Text only; the trigger is already a button.

elements.summary: The panel of an item. Its height animates.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.notes: Grid wrapper whose row animates between 0fr and 1fr.

anatomy.name: inner
anatomy.notes: Clips the content while it animates.

anatomy.name: body
anatomy.notes: Holds the bottom padding, so a closed panel collapses to zero height.

useCases.when: Independent topics where reading one at a time is enough

antiPatterns.why: The trigger is a button; nested controls break keyboard and screen reader use
Opening one item opens the others with the same value
antiPatterns.alternative: Give every item a unique value

coverage: heading around a native button named by its text; level prop
single: opening closes others; collapsible closes the open item
non-collapsible single: open trigger aria-disabled, stays open
change detail, bubbles, composed, not fired for code changes; a slotted control's change has no detail
Arrow Up/Down wrap, Home/End, tab order intact
disabled item skipped; disabled accordion dims every trigger
ariaControlsElements and region named by trigger (accessibility tree)
focus ring keyboard-only in token color
height transition from token; none under reduced motion
content or trigger added later is wired (aria-controls, region name)
level clamped to 2-6; whitespace in an item value warns once

drift.realization: the visual reference uses a translucent ring below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11)

drift.contract: arrow keys, Home, End between triggers; all triggers tabbable
drift.realization: added to the reference's markup following the APG; plain focus management, not the roving-focus controller, because triggers must stay in the tab order
ElementInternals ariaLabelledByElements; aria-label copy of the trigger text where unsupported

coverage: Accordion: 6 variant(s), State (Rest, Focus) x Open (False, True) x Disabled (False, True); read back ok

openQuestions.question: How is value expressed for selection=multiple?
openQuestions.answer: A space-separated string in the attribute; the event detail carries a string[].

openQuestions.question: Roving tabindex or all triggers in the tab order?
openQuestions.answer: All triggers stay in the tab order and arrows add shortcuts (APG accordion); plain focus management, not the roving-focus controller.

openQuestions.question: Heading level?
openQuestions.answer: A level prop on the trigger (default 3) rendered as role=heading with aria-level.

openQuestions.question: Event name?
openQuestions.answer: value-change, not change, so native change events from controls inside the content are not confused with it.

openQuestions.question: Open item of a non-collapsible single accordion?
openQuestions.answer: Keep its trigger focusable with aria-disabled=true (APG).
